tasks.title: Add the plain net10.0 TFM to DungeonMaster.App and create the DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests project with its AppFixture

Neither body throws. Its XML doc comment states that every future Platforms/ seam now needs a third body or the bare TFM breaks.

This is a measured trap: `_ = platformView;` made `AppSource_NoLineStatesADiscardedTask` fail during the spike.

The XAML source generator runs for the bare TFM. Built with `-p:EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles=true -p:CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath=<scratch>`, the number of `.xsg.cs` files produced EQUALS the number of shared `.xaml` files in the App project, and the number of those `.xsg.cs` files containing `InitializeComponent` equals the same figure. tasks.title: RepoPaths: require src/DungeonMaster.App beneath the ancestor, and make the walk testable (MASTER-008)
acceptance: The public surface in contracts/repo-paths.md section 1 is byte-identical in signature: `Root`, `AppRoot`, `AppSourceFiles(string)`. No member is renamed, no accessibility changes, no required member is added. Evidence: the 37 referencing lines across 16 files still compile, shown by `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj -v m` printing `0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)`. The walk accepts an ancestor only when it contains BOTH a `.git` entry AND a `src/DungeonMaster.App` directory, and keeps walking upward otherwise. Both the `.git`-as-a-directory and the `.git`-as-a-file forms are accepted; the linked-worktree form is the layout every task in this session actually runs in, and narrowing back to `Directory.Exists` is a regression.

`src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/RepoPathsTests.cs` exists and discriminates the three accept/reject layouts named in contracts/repo-paths.md section 5, each built in a temporary directory rather than against the real checkout: (a) `.git` directory plus `src/DungeonMaster.App` accepted; (b) `.git` FILE plus `src/DungeonMaster.App` accepted; (c) an inner ancestor with a `.git` entry and NO `src/DungeonMaster.App`, beneath an outer one that has both — the OUTER is returned. A fourth test establishes the error path: no ancestor satisfies both conditions, and an `InvalidOperationException` is thrown whose message contains the directory the walk started from and names both conditions it was looking for.

Each of the four tests is shown able to fail, by a red step or a demonstrated discrimination, with the command and the observed failure quoted. For case (c) specifically, the report shows the test failing against the walk's pre-task acceptance condition (`.git` entry only) — that is the discrimination that proves the new condition is what the test is reading.

`AppSourceFiles` still returns absolute paths under `AppRoot` with `obj/` and `bin/` segments excluded, ordinal-ascending, and returns an EMPTY LIST rather than throwing or asserting when the pattern matches nothing. A test covers the empty-pattern case; per contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 1, non-emptiness is the caller's guard and never this helper's.

`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj` passes. The new count is stated with the command, together with the number of tests this task added, and the two are shown to account for the difference from the 640 baseline.

tasks.title: ThemeSource: XDocument object model, helpers stop asserting, shared comment/line-number/character-entity helpers (MASTER-028 core, MASTER-102, MASTER-138, MASTER-040 helper)
acceptance: Every member listed in contracts/theme-source.md section 1 survives with its signature AND its semantics unchanged, `LegacyTolerantKeyDefinitionPattern` included. GeometryScaleTests already depends on this; a shortening implementation silently breaks every line number it reports.

`BlankCSharpComments` adopts the ANCHORED pattern form, and its XML doc comment records why, citing `GeometryScaleTests.WholeLineCommentPattern` by name. This resolves the disagreement between the two existing copies, `ThemeDictionaryTests.CSharpLineCommentPattern` and `ThemeTokenParityTests.CommentLine`. [AMENDED E5 (retrospective, FIFTH occurrence), 2026-09-02: this criterion carried the same wrong citation as T7's criterion 7 - `GeometryScaleTests.cs:727-730`, which is inside a method body. It was not in the orchestrator's list of E5 sites and was found by sweeping the artifacts for the bad string after amending the listed ones. The real declaration is `WholeLineCommentPattern` at `:845`; `grep -n "private static readonly Regex.*CommentPattern =" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/GeometryScaleTests.cs` returns `838` and `845`. T3 landed at `ea06a76` and its implementer used the right pattern regardless, so nothing was misdirected.]

`DecodeCharacterEntities` handles BOTH the decimal (`←`) and hex (`←`) entity forms and uses `char.ConvertFromUtf32`, and `IsSingleRune` counts Runes rather than chars. A test asserts `DecodeCharacterEntities("🛡")` returns a two-char string whose single Rune value is 0x1F6E1, and that `IsSingleRune` returns true for it. A test asserts reference identity for one such file across the two calls. This is MASTER-068 answered at the ThemeSource level.

No member of ThemeSource constructs a `Regex` inside a loop or per call; every pattern is a `static readonly` field. This is MASTER-063 at this level, with the cited authority https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/base-types/compilation-and-reuse-in-regular-expressions.

`src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/ThemeSourceScanGuardTests.cs` holds one named `[Fact]` per ThemeSource scan (`ThemeFiles`, `ThemeDocuments`, `AppDocuments`, `KeyedElements`), each asserting non-emptiness of exactly that scan and nothing else, named per contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 2, and carrying forward the `because` string already written at the retired site where one exists.
Every new test is shown able to fail, by a red step or a demonstrated discrimination, with the command named and the observed failure quoted per test.

`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj` passes; the count is stated with the command and the difference from 640 is accounted for. No consuming class is edited by this task — `git status --porcelain -- <this task's owns globs>` is quoted to show only this task's four files changed. [AMENDED E7, 2026-09-02: `git diff --name-only` was the wrong command and this is a measured defect, not a style note. It omits UNTRACKED files entirely - three of T3's four deliverables were new files, so it listed none of them - and unscoped in a shared worktree it reported five files belonging to other tasks. `git status --porcelain -- <this task's owns globs>` lists tracked and untracked alike and scopes peer work away.] This amendment is retrospective: T3 landed at `ea06a76` before the defect was found, and its reviewer raised it.
Every file is tab-indented CRLF, verified per file by comparing `tr -cd '\r' | wc -c` against `tr -cd '\n' | wc -c`. Neither grep line-ending form appears in the evidence.

The whole `RegexOptions.Compiled` surface under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/` is SURVEYED and the survey is published in this task's report as the inventory T4, T7 and T9 work from. `grep -rn "RegexOptions.Compiled" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App --include=*.cs | wc -l` returns 64 today across 13 files (`grep -rc "RegexOptions.Compiled" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App --include=*.cs | grep -v ':0$'`), and `grep -rn "new Regex(" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App --include=*.cs` finds 6 method-body construction sites: `BindablePropertyDefaultsMatchTokensTests.cs:84, :129`; `DmThemeKeysResolveTests.cs:136`; `ThemeDictionaryTests.cs:304, :308, :358`. That is TWO MORE than MASTER-063's `locations` list names (`:358` and `DmThemeKeysResolveTests.cs:136` are absent from it). The task re-derives every one of these figures with those commands and quotes them; it inherits none.

The rule the survey establishes, and which T3 satisfies inside `ThemeSource.cs`: `RegexOptions.Compiled` survives ONLY on a pattern held in a `static readonly` field that lives for the process. Every pattern constructed inside a method body either drops the flag or is hoisted to such a field. Authority: https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/base-types/compilation-and-reuse-in-regular-expressions - the flag raises construction cost to lower match cost, so a short-lived compiled `Regex` pays the cost and collects none of the benefit. T3 fixes only sites inside files it owns; the six method-body sites live in T4's and T9's files and are their criteria. That division is deliberate: it is what keeps each half checkable by the task that owns it.

tasks.title: Theme dictionary, token parity and implicit style facts: onto the XDocument model, guards promoted, loop-constructed regexes hoisted (MASTER-028, MASTER-063, MASTER-102, MASTER-138)

It closed on the first `</Style>` with `.*?`, so a nested style mis-terminated the body and attributed its setters to the wrong target; the replacement reads `Style` elements and their `Setter` children as XML, which cannot mis-terminate. A test demonstrates the difference against a synthetic document containing a nested `Style` — the report quotes the old pattern's wrong answer and the new reader's right one.

The three assertion sites inside non-test helpers are retired: `ImplicitStyleTests.cs:204` (in `Styles()`, declared :186), `ThemeDictionaryTests.cs:369` (in `MergedThemeSourcesInAppXaml()`, :350), `ThemeTokenParityTests.cs:158` (in `ResourceKeyDefinitions()`, :142). A fact whose mechanism changed and that was never seen failing afterwards has not been shown to still test anything.

No offenders-list fact rests on `BeEmpty` alone: per contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 5, each such fact is paired with a guard on the scan that produced the list, because an offenders list is empty both when everything is correct and when nothing was examined.

`dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj` passes with the count stated with its command and the difference from the previous run accounted for. `git status --porcelain -- <this task's owns globs>` shows only this task's four files changed, tracked and untracked alike. `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/TokenNamingTests.cs` gains its own non-emptiness guard. It consumes `ThemeSource.ThemeFiles()` at :305, `ThemeSource.XmlCommentPattern` at :308 and :581, and `ThemeSource.ThemeFileText("Tokens.xaml")` at :582 - re-derive with `grep -n "ThemeSource\." src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/TokenNamingTests.cs` and quote it. This file is explicitly owned and explicitly guarded from here on. [CORRECTED (retrospective), 2026-09-02: this criterion said that when T3 removed the assertion from `ThemeFiles()`, the file would lose "its only vacuity protection and nothing else in the session replaces it". That is FALSE and was measured false twice - by T4 and independently by T4's reviewer. The claim was the architect's, made at Gate 2, and it is what justified extending T4's ownership to this file. The distinction that survives: `TokenNamingTests`'s guards sat INSIDE ITS FACTS, so retiring the helper assertion cost it nothing, whereas `DmThemeKeysResolveTests`'s guards sit inside private helpers with no in-fact backup - which is why contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 1.1 row 16 genuinely is load-bearing and this file's rows never were. See contracts/theme-source.md section 3 for the full correction.] A named guard `[Fact]` per contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 2 is added HERE, asserting that the file collection THIS CLASS scans is non-empty. This covers `ThemeDictionaryTests.cs:304` and `:308` (inside the `foreach (var style in styleKeys)` loop) and `:358` (constructed per call of `MergedThemeSourcesInAppXaml`), the last of which MASTER-063's `locations` list does not name. `grep -n "new Regex("` over each owned file is quoted before and after, against T3's published survey.

tasks.title: Accessibility scan: rune-correct entity decoding and an XML-based control scan (MASTER-040, MASTER-028, MASTER-138)
acceptance: The local `Decode` at SemanticDescriptionTests.cs:222-235 is gone and the class calls `ThemeSource.DecodeCharacterEntities`. `grep -n "(char)int.Parse" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Accessibility/SemanticDescriptionTests.cs` returns nothing, and that command and its empty result are quoted. This is half of MASTER-040; T3 owns the shared helper and its unit tests.

`IsIconOnly` (:243) no longer tests `text.Length != 1`. It uses `ThemeSource.IsSingleRune` and classifies the single Rune's Unicode category. A supplementary-plane private-use or symbol codepoint is therefore classified as icon-only under ITS OWN codepoint, rather than under the truncated BMP value the `char` cast produced. [AMENDED, 2026-09-02: the words "rejected outright" and "dropped" overstated the defect and this criterion inherited the audit's account of it. T5's reviewer MEASURED what the `(char)` cast actually does: it turns `U+1F6E1` into `U+F6E1`, a LENGTH-1 PRIVATE-USE string, which `text.Length != 1` ACCEPTS. So the old scan REACHED that control and reported it under a codepoint it does not have - it was MISREPORTED, not dropped. A genuine drop needs a form the old hex-only entity regex could not decode at all. The delivered code and its injection are sound and nothing about T5's verdict changes; `de371fb`'s commit message inherited the same error and cannot be rewritten, and `reviews/T5.md` carries the correction.]

The report shows this test failing against the pre-task `(char)`-cast and `Length != 1` implementation, with the command and the observed failure quoted. That is the discrimination for this entry and it is arithmetic, not a suppression interaction, so it cannot be satisfied by a second mechanism. The failure the test must show is the control being examined under the WRONG codepoint, not the control going unexamined. [AMENDED, 2026-09-02: the words "rejected outright" and "dropped" overstated the defect and this criterion inherited the audit's account of it. T5's reviewer MEASURED what the `(char)` cast actually does: it turns `U+1F6E1` into `U+F6E1`, a LENGTH-1 PRIVATE-USE string, which `text.Length != 1` ACCEPTS. So the old scan REACHED that control and reported it under a codepoint it does not have - it was MISREPORTED, not dropped. A genuine drop needs a form the old hex-only entity regex could not decode at all. The delivered code and its injection are sound and nothing about T5's verdict changes; `de371fb`'s commit message inherited the same error and cannot be rewritten, and `reviews/T5.md` carries the correction.]

The `ControlTag` regex at :31-34 is replaced by an XML-based scan over `ThemeSource.AppDocuments()`. Its `[^>]*?` attribute match truncated any tag whose attribute value contained `>`, and its sibling `TextAttribute` at :36-39 saw only double-quoted attributes, so a single-quoted `Text='...'` was invisible. A test demonstrates that a control the old scan could not reach is now examined — the report quotes both the old scan's miss and the new scan's hit.

The inline line-number computation at :112-115 (`source.Take(tag.Index).Count(c => c == '\n') + 1`, whose `.Take(tag.Index)` is at line 113) is gone, replaced by the line info the XML model carries or by `ThemeSource.LineNumber`. `grep -n "Take(tag.Index)" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Accessibility/SemanticDescriptionTests.cs` returns nothing, quoted, and the report confirms no other inline `Count(c => c == '\n')` remains in the file. This is one of the three identical copies MASTER-138 names.

`PendingDescription` (:62) is preserved as the allow list it is, and this task neither empties it nor adds to it. If migrating the scan makes a previously-unreached control visible and it has no description, the task escalates rather than adding it to the allow list — silently widening an allow list to keep a fact green is the failure mode this whole session is about.

The class's existing anti-vacuity assertions (:138, :151, :203) are preserved in force. Any that has moved into a non-test helper is promoted to a named guard `[Fact]` per contracts/anti-vacuity.md section 2; any that is already inside a `[Fact]` stays where it is, because that is the correct place and moving it would be churn.

Every fact in the class still passes and, where its mechanism changed, is shown able to fail with the command and the observed failure quoted. `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj` passes with the count stated with its command.

tasks.title: Icon font coverage: extract and exercise the TrueType cmap parser, cache the scan, share the decoder (MASTER-101, MASTER-068, MASTER-040, MASTER-138)
acceptance: The `TrueTypeCmap` parser is no longer a nested private class inside a fact about icons. It is a named `internal static class TrueTypeCmap` in its own file `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/App/Theme/TrueTypeCmap.cs`, with `Codepoints(byte[] font)` as its entry point. Its behaviour for the real font is unchanged: the two named codepoints the app depends on, 0xEA8F and 0xEAD4, are still reported as covered.

MASTER-101 is closed one of the two ways the audit offers, and the report says which and why. The version chosen is recorded in `Directory.Packages.props` with a comment naming the server version it was proven against and the date, and the report quotes the session-open output that proves it.
